key_insight: SGD in a two-layer ReLU network can learn a shortcut spurious feature before the true XOR signal, and strong spurious correlation can suppress signal learning.
engineering_relevance: This work explains why overparameterized classifiers may lock onto easy but misleading cues, informing more robust training and dataset design.
method: Theoretical end-to-end analysis of online minibatch SGD on logistic loss.
Two-layer ReLU network trained on high-dimensional Boolean hypercube data with XOR signal and linear spurious correlation.
Derives phase transitions showing exponential early spurious-feature growth and delayed signal learning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical characterization, with the strongest spurious correlation case showing domination even at the XOR sample-complexity threshold, plus preliminary empirical evidence for eventual XOR learning when correlation is constant.
watch_item: Results are strongest in the specified Boolean/XOR setting, so generalization to other architectures, losses, or real-world datasets may be limited.
paper_title: SGD Provably Prioritizes a Shortcut Spurious Feature in the XOR Model
